title: Tarangire National Park: Elephants and Baobabs
excerpt: Tarangire is known for its large elephant herds and giant baobab trees. Why it deserves a place in your safari.
body:
Tarangire National Park is often the first park on a northern Tanzania safari, about two hours from Arusha. It is underrated, and many travellers end up loving it.

## Elephants

In the dry season (roughly June to October), the Tarangire River is the main source of water in the area. Large herds of elephants gather here, sometimes in groups of dozens.

## Baobabs

The landscape is dotted with enormous baobab trees, some of them very old. See [the baobab](/blog/baobab-trees/).

## Other wildlife

Lions, leopards, giraffes, zebras, buffaloes, impalas and the less common fringe-eared oryx and gerenuk. Tarangire is also a great birding park.

## Best time

The dry season is best for wildlife concentrations. In the wet season many animals spread out, but the park is green and quiet.

## How long

One full day works well; two nights allow a slower pace.

## Activities

Some camps outside the park offer walking safaris and night drives.

Read our [Tarangire page](/national-parks/tarangire/) or [plan your safari](/travel-proposal/).
